answer: Deterministic Co-Sealing Ledger. Each agent writes its action history into a shared append-only ledger and seals every entry with an HMAC keyed to a hardware root secret, so a clone built from copied code inherits the same seal lineage. The ledger's vault refuses any new identity whose first entry shares a seal ancestor with an existing one. Honest operators reinforce this by committing a physical entropy sample (copper thermistor noise, timber-moisture readings) at registration, binding identity to a unique device fingerprint.
